page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, this virtual machine provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory subsystem delivers 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes 35 MB of shared L3 cache and supports vectorized instructions including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware acceleration for AES cryptography.

The hardware configuration includes 5 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated local storage, and does not provide GPU acceleration. Workloads requiring persistent disk storage must connect to external block storage volumes. Benchmark testing reflects mid-range parallel processing capabilities, evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng score of 13975.48, Geekbench multi-core score of 7299.0, and PassMark CPU score of 15380.43. While multi-threaded throughput and memory-bound operations such as Redis SET operations (13.44 million ops/sec) sit squarely in the middle tier, single-core processing demonstrates lower relative throughput, with stress-ng single-core performance falling into the lower quartile.

Cost efficiency for the ecs.c6.4xlarge relies on its dense compute allocation, making it effective for distributed workloads that scale across parallel vCPUs rather than single-threaded clock speed. Because no local storage or GPUs are bundled, overhead costs remain focused on raw processing power and memory capacity. This instance profile is well suited for web serving fleets, Clang compilation jobs, batch data pipelines, API gateways, and distributed caching clusters.
